h1: Digital Experiences — Agencies & Studios Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference built around “Crafted Digital Experiences Built to Outlast Trends”, with the layout, timings and palette written down in the brief.
summary: Landing page reference for an agency or studio — a stats row, Instrument Serif, React and Tailwind CSS and a word-by-word headline.
about: Digital Experiences is the landing page reference for an agency or studio, and the brief behind it is a full build spec rather than a mood board. The page's own headline reads “Crafted Digital Experiences Built to Outlast Trends”, and the composition is built around those exact words. The colour scheme is black #0D0D0C underneath, and the page is set in Instrument Serif. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 640x458 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Motion comes down to 500ms transitions. Keep it open while you write: the 8,994-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: Links before the action
layout.body: The bar is one row of text and one action, measured at 10px spacing steps and 500ms transitions so it reads as a strip rather than as a band. The bar sits over the 640x458 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: One family, two roles
layout.body: The faces are assigned roles rather than mixed: Instrument Serif carries the display and the interface together. Tracking is set per size, so the display line and the caption do not share one letter-spacing value. One family with clear roles beats two that compete.

layout.title: The nav is deliberately thin
layout.body: The wordmark holds the left edge and the links run to the right of it, all of it set in Instrument Serif so the bar belongs to the page below rather than to a separate system.

layout.title: Numbers carried into the build
layout.body: Type and spacing are drawn from one list here: 10px spacing steps and 500ms transitions. The smallest and largest values in that list set the range the composition works in.

motion.title: The whole animation budget
motion.body: The brief fixes the transition value at 500ms, so a rebuild cannot substitute a slower default. The quoted timing covers state changes, so the feedback is the part of the motion that is specified.

motion.title: Scroll drives the sequence
motion.body: Scroll reveal is the page's single scroll behaviour, so the effect has a defined place in the composition. It is a handful of lines rather than a scroll library, which keeps the rebuild light.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over black #0D0D0C, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.
notes: The reference was captured at 640x458, and every value quoted on this page comes from the same brief.
The timing budget is state feedback rather than page choreography (500ms), so a slower rebuild reads as a different design.

editorial.title: How Digital Experiences sequences the first read
editorial.body: A page like this usually buries the action under a feature grid. This one puts navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the client row in a fixed sequence, with the action inside the first screen rather than after three scroll lengths. A agency reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: What moves in Digital Experiences
editorial.body: The trade-off is that nothing here rewards a second look for its animation. What it rewards is the reading order, with 500ms transitions, a word-by-word headline and a scroll reveal confirming state rather than decorating it. Nothing animates for its own sake in this landing page.

editorial.title: The numbers behind the landing page
editorial.body: When a rebuild drifts, the spacing goes first. Digital Experiences avoids that by publishing 10px spacing steps and 500ms transitions with the composition. Nothing in this landing page depends on a default.

faq.question: What do I get when I copy the Digital Experiences brief?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 640x458, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: Can I rebuild the Digital Experiences landing page in a different stack?
faq.answer: Digital Experiences was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Where did the Digital Experiences design come from?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 640x458.
